title: 3 Questions on Cut Groups
extended_summary:
This paper is a theoretical mathematics article about finite group theory, not an education study. It investigates three open questions about cut groups, also called inverse semi-rational groups, and their structural properties.

The first question asks whether the degrees of the fields generated by character table entries are uniformly bounded across all cut groups. The paper notes known positive results for solvable cut groups and for quasi-simple or almost simple groups, while also contrasting these with related classes where the answer is negative.

The second question concerns whether Sylow 3-subgroups of cut groups are themselves cut. The paper reviews partial positive results from prior work for several classes of groups, including solvable, Frobenius, odd-order, and quasi/simple groups. The third question asks whether certain normal p-subgroups in solvable cut groups have exponent dividing p for p in {5,7}. The paper mainly synthesizes existing results and poses open problems; it does not report an intervention, participants, or empirical outcomes.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a pure mathematics/theory paper on cut groups and character tables, with no educational technology intervention, no K-12 context, and no empirical study design. It is not evidence about AI-supported science inquiry or student outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: There is no educational or learner impact reported, and no intervention effects are evaluated. The paper has no direct relevance to K-12 learning outcomes or technology implementation.
